primitives.name: Motion Is Pass Indicator
primitives.verbatim_quote: ## Motion -> pass, overwhelmingly - pass rate with motion: **0.999** (1,765 of 1,766 plays) - pass rate without: **0.650** - chi-square **p = 2.8e-205** Motion nearly *entails* a pass in this dataset.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'P(pass|motion)': 'probability of pass given motion, dimensionless', 'P(pass|¬motion)': 'probability of pass without motion, dimensionless', 'χ²': 'chi-square test statistic, dimensionless'}
primitives.assumptions: Data is representative of NFL play patterns; motion flag is accurate and complete at snap time.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When motion flag is absent, pass probability reverts to baseline 0.650.

layer2.mapping: Motion flag maps to a probabilistic pass event selector in GSI; in GSE, it acts as a deterministic pass-state trigger.
layer2.telemetry: Pass rate accuracy under motion condition.

primitives.name: Motion Predicts Coverage None
primitives.verbatim_quote: ## Motion -> coverage, still nothing - 8-class `team_coverage_type` distribution, motion vs not: p = **0.128**; shares are near-identical (Cover 1: 20.0% vs 20.5%, Cover 3: 36.9% vs 36.0%).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'P(coverage|motion)': 'probability of coverage type given motion, dimensionless', 'P(coverage)': 'baseline probability of coverage type, dimensionless', 'p': 'p-value of chi-square test, dimensionless'}
primitives.assumptions: Coverage types are independent of motion flag; data is balanced across coverage classes.
primitives.breakdown_regime: No significant difference in coverage class distribution between motion and non-motion plays.

layer2.mapping: Motion flag is orthogonal to coverage type in GSI; in GSE, it is a null predictor for coverage decisions.
layer2.telemetry: Chi-square test p-value for coverage class equality.

primitives.name: Motion As Filter
primitives.verbatim_quote: So its job in a pipeline is as a **filter** (select the pass subset, ~100% purity, instead of 65%) and as a *sample-selection device for tracking work*, not as a coverage predictor.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'Filter_motion(X)': 'set of plays filtered by motion flag, dimensionless', 'purity': 'fraction of passes in filtered set, dimensionless'}
primitives.assumptions: Motion flag is a sufficient condition for pass event; filtering improves signal-to-noise ratio.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Motion-based filtering increases pass detection purity from 0.65 to 1.0.

layer2.mapping: In GSI, motion filters for pass events; in GSE, it selects a substate for further tracking.

reasoning_traces.think:
Motion is a strong predictive signal for pass events, with a near-certain conditional probability of 0.999. This implies a high-information content for distinguishing pass from run. The statistical significance (p = 2.8e-205) confirms that motion is not a random occurrence but a structured signal. In contrast, motion shows no statistically significant effect on coverage type (p = 0.128), indicating that while motion predicts pass, it does not predict defensive alignment. This duality suggests motion operates in two distinct domains: one for event classification (pass vs run), and another for no-op in coverage prediction. The failure mode lies in assuming motion encodes coverage information, which is not supported by empirical data. The motion flag is a binary pre-snap feature, thus cannot capture reactive behaviors post-snap, limiting its use in dynamic tracking models. It functions as a high-fidelity gate for pass events, enabling downstream analysis to focus on relevant subsets rather than full datasets.
